findings.description: Step 8 has a single implementer subagent fix the CI findings "and push", but implementers work on their own branch and worktree (step 4), and step 8 never says to merge that branch into the integration branch. Read literally, the push sends nothing new and the fixes never reach the PR. Suggested wording: "merge it into the integration branch with a **merger subagent**, and push".

Step 3's `gh pr create --draft` has no `--base`, so `gh` targets the GitHub default branch. `pr-description` passes `--base <trunk>` (`GIT_TRUNK`). When `GIT_TRUNK` differs from the default branch, the draft opens against the wrong base. Suggested wording: `gh pr create --draft --base <trunk>`.

The new clause ("which `scripts/pre-commit` runs, and the `Stop` hook too, tests aside, and the workflows under `.github/workflows/`") is accurate but hard to parse: "tests aside" sits between two "and" clauses, so a reader can take it to apply to the workflows. Splitting it helps, e.g. "which `scripts/pre-commit` runs (the `Stop` hook runs them too, except `TEST_CMD`), and the workflows under `.github/workflows/`".

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer used one tool call and judged from the diff alone. It never Read the changed files, so the `.claude/rules` injection of docs/conventions never fired and it checked only against AGENTS.md. On a 15-line prose/bash delta the impact is low, but the convention coverage for this round is shallow.
